text: The Beneficiary satisfies 8 C.F.R. §204.5(h)(3)(v) by demonstrating original contributions of major significance in the field of weightlifting through innovative methodologies, institutional leadership, and international impact.

The Beneficiary developed the original Body Alignment Training (BAT) methodology, which integrates traditional Chinese bone-setting theories with modern sports science to improve posture, movement mechanics, and injury prevention [Exhibit A1, p.2].

This innovative system employs a structured three-layer progression focusing on elasticity with resistance for body-weight power, strength with resistance for core stability, and alignment and space restoration for rebalancing the body [Exhibit B1, p.2].

The BAT program reflects the Beneficiary's deep concern for athlete health and has been implemented globally, with specific applications such as a knee protection training model that reduced knee injury rates by 32% in a weightlifting coach training camp [Exhibit B5, p.3].

This methodology represents a significant departure from traditional weightlifting training that focuses solely on strength, mobility, or power, establishing a comprehensive approach that has been adopted by international fitness institutions [Exhibit B1, p.2].

Furthermore, the Beneficiary's BAT methodology has produced demonstrable results for elite international athletes, including Olympic medalists and national team members from multiple countries [Exhibit A1, p.2].

Following training under the Beneficiary's guidance, Indonesian athletes including Eko Yuli Irawan, a frequent Summer Olympics medal recipient, and Luluk Diana Tri Wijayana, who won gold medals at the XXI National Sports Week in 2024, achieved significant competitive success [Exhibit B1, p.2].

The President of the Indonesian Weightlifting Federation East Java Province, who has been involved in weightlifting for approximately 20 years, specifically chose to bring athletes to train with the Beneficiary due to her exceptional competence in enhancing performance [Exhibit B1, p.2].

Three-time Olympic Gold Medalist Xiaojun Lyu has personally witnessed the Beneficiary's contributions to athlete performance and health improvement, noting that her holistic approach has helped countless athletes address body alignment issues and achieve greater success in international competitions [Exhibit B3, p.2].

In addition to her methodological innovations, the Beneficiary founded Venus Weightlifting Club (VWC) in 2015, establishing China's first amateur weightlifting club and pioneering a new model for weightlifting participation outside the traditional national team system [Exhibit A1, p.2].

This club successfully filled a critical gap in China's weightlifting landscape by providing standardized training access to amateur enthusiasts, teenagers, and fitness enthusiasts who previously lacked professional training channels [Exhibit B4, p.2].

The club's significance is recognized by industry leaders including Chong Peng, General Manager of Donnor Exhibition, which organizes the influential IWF Health, Wellness, Fitness Expo—one of China's largest and most extensive fitness industry exhibitions [Exhibit B4, p.2].

Under the Beneficiary's leadership, VWC has developed into a leading institution in China's fitness industry with multiple training venues and a powerful coaching team that provides scientific, systematic weightlifting training [Exhibit B4, p.2].

Moreover, the Beneficiary created and organized the ALL Stars Weightlifting event, which has been successfully held for eight sessions since its establishment and has become one of the most influential events in China's amateur weightlifting development [Exhibit B3, p.2].

This event attracts contestants from 32 provinces and cities throughout China and has reached international standards in scale, competition level, and organizational professionalism [Exhibit B3, p.2].

In 2019 alone, the event featured multiple competition levels covering different weight groups from 55kg to 105kg and attracted 185 contestants, including 10 national or international athletes alongside amateur enthusiasts nationwide [Exhibit B3, p.2].

Additionally, the Beneficiary organized the 'Venus Weightlifting Challenge & Amateur Weightlifting Championships,' which attracts more than 200 contestants annually, and hosted the 'VENUS LIFFOFF Forum' in 2021, inviting global weightlifting champions and experts to discuss weightlifting popularization [Exhibit B4, p.3].

Beyond domestic initiatives, the Beneficiary has established significant international partnerships, including collaborations with the Singapore Weightlifting Federation, whose President, Tom Liaw, serves as an Executive Board Member of the International Weightlifting Federation and Vice President of the Commonwealth Weightlifting Federation [Exhibit B2, p.2].

Through these partnerships, the Beneficiary has supported multiple international and local weightlifting events, leveraging her extensive social media following to bolster their visibility and success [Exhibit B2, p.2].

She has facilitated connections with international brands such as Cluster, Anta, and Luxiaojun, securing sponsorships for weightlifting equipment and apparel that have significantly enhanced athletes' training facilities and preparation quality [Exhibit B2, p.2].

Furthermore, the Beneficiary has played a critical role in identifying and nurturing promising young weightlifters, leveraging her network and resources to help federations recruit talent and provide development opportunities [Exhibit B2, p.2].

Consequently, the Beneficiary's training system has produced quantifiable competitive success, with more than 20 students winning medals in competitions worldwide, including 12 athletes who have entered the professional arena and become vital new forces in the global weightlifting industry [Exhibit B4, p.3].

Her methodology has been implemented through partnerships with leading fitness institutions such as OneFit, China's pioneering coach training system founded in 2011, which has cumulatively trained over 200,000 coaches and adopted training courses by many international fitness institutions [Exhibit B5, p.2].

As an internal weightlifting trainer for OneFit, the Beneficiary trains coaches to master the latest techniques and theories, introducing core concepts of body alignment and injury prevention that enable more professional and comprehensive guidance [Exhibit B5, p.2].

Her BAT methodology has been adopted by multiple international fitness institutions, including the Singapore Weightlifting Federation, the Brunei national team weightlifters, and the Indonesian national team athletes, demonstrating its global applicability and effectiveness [Exhibit B5, p.3].

Finally, the Beneficiary has received formal recognition from prestigious industry associations, including individual membership in the Shanghai Fitness Bodybuilding Association, a professional non-profit industrial organization founded in 2004 that formulates standards for Shanghai municipal gymnasiums [Exhibit C2, p.2].

Her membership application underwent rigorous review by Chong Peng, Vice President of the Association and a top fitness and bodybuilding expert in China, who certified that the Beneficiary had been devoting herself to fitness teaching promotion for over 10 years since 2015 [Exhibit C2, p.3].

The Association's membership criteria require applicants to have been engaged in the fitness industry for more than 10 years or be senior practitioners serving as senior management of famous enterprises in the industry, with membership reserved for those with outstanding achievements [Exhibit C2, p.3].

Furthermore, the Association has published industry standards including 'The Star Level Evaluation Standard Implementation Outline for Commercial Fitness Service Gymnasiums in Shanghai' and 'The Professional Skill Level Evaluation Standard Implementation Outline for Fitness Coaches in Shanghai,' contributing to the standardization and professionalization of the fitness industry in which the Beneficiary operates [Exhibit C3, p.9].

In sum, the foregoing evidence clearly establishes that the Beneficiary's original contributions have substantially advanced the field of weightlifting through methodological innovation, athlete development, and industry-wide recognition.
